'''Kirthi Tennakone''' is a Sri Lankan scientist with an assortment of research interests in theoretical and experimental physics, chemistry and biological systems. He has authored over 350 publications covering a diverse variety of disciplines. He is the former Director of Institute of Fundamental Studies, Sri Lanka (now named as National Institute of Fundamental Studies) and the first Professor of Physics at the University of Ruhuna, Sri Lanka. He pursued studies leading to a doctoral degree in Theoretical Physics at the University of Hawaiʻi under supervision of Sandip Pakvasa. Pakvasa and Tennakone were the first to suggest that neutrinos may be massive<ref name=":0" /> and to consider the astrophysical implications. In [[condensed matter physics]], Tennakone pioneered the studies on semiconducting properties copper(I) thiocyanate,<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /> a rare example of a transparent p-type semiconductor, currently adopted in many devices and developed techniques of its deposition as thin films. He was the first to introduce the concept of the dye-sensitized solid state solar<ref name="Tennekone 1995 1689–1693">{{Cite journal|last=Tennekone |display-authors=etal|first=K.|year=1995|title=A dye-sensitized nano-porous solid-state photovoltaic cell|journal=Semiconductor Science and Technology|volume=10|issue=12|pages=1689–1693|doi=10.1088/0268-1242/10/12/020|bibcode=1995SeScT..10.1689T|s2cid=250896378 }}</ref> cell and demonstrate a working prototype of the same. Sri Lanka Government recognized his contribution to research and education and awarded National Honors on [[Deshabandu|two occasions]]. He was one of the [[Union of Concerned Scientists]] who signed to the document presented to world leaders in 1992 about [[environmental degradation]] that threatens global life support systems on this planet.

==Early life==
{{BLP unsourced section |date=June 2019}}
Born 1940 in a Village in Sri Lanka near the town of [[Veyangoda]], he was exposed rural environment in early childhood.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nifs.ac.lk/about/director/professor-kirthi-tennakone|title = Professor Kirthi Tennakone &#124; National Institute of Fundamental Studies (NIFS), Sri Lanka}}</ref>  He is a son of the poet and writer Piyathilaka Tennakone of [[Metitotumulla]], Sri Lanka who inspired him to science and mathematics at an early stage. Kirthi Tennakone received primary education at [[Bandaranayake Central College, Veyangoda|the Central College, Veyangoda]], Sri Lanka.

==Education==
He earned a B.S in physics and mathematics from the [[University of Ceylon]] 1964. After serving as a teacher in the Department of Education for period of four years, he received an East-West Center Fellowship to pursue studies at the [[University of Hawaiʻi]] and obtained a PhD degree in [[theoretical physics]] in 1972. He returned to Sri Lanka accepting an academic position at the University of Jayewardenepura and later appointed to the Chair of Physics at the [[University of Ruhuna]]. When the first endowed Chair in Sri Lanka (Sumanasekara Chair in Natural Science) was commissioned at the Institute of Fundamental Studies, he was appointed to this position by the [[President of Sri Lanka]] on basis of the recommendation of a high ranking search committee. Subsequently, he served as the director of this institution for a period of thirteen years, concurrently holding a professorship.

He has held visiting research positions at the [[International Centre for Theoretical Physics|International Center for Theoretical Physics]], Trieste; [[Niels Bohr Institute]], Copenhagen; Japan Society for Promotion of Science, Invitation Fellowship at the [[Shizuoka University]], Japan; [[University of Cincinnati]] and currently an adjunct professor of physics at [[Georgia State University]].

==Recognition==
Kirthi Tennakone has been awarded National Honors of the Government of Sri Lanka on two occasions, "[[Vidya Nidhi]]" in 1986 and "[[Deshabandu|Desha Bandu]]" in 2005. [[University of Sri Jayewardenepura]] of Sri Lanka conferred an Honorary [[Doctor of Science]] Degree to him in 2007. He is a Fellow of [[The World Academy of Sciences]], elected 1990. He was one of the invited scholars to visit Solar Cell Materials & Devices Group, Beijing, China.

==Research==
''Neutrino Physics'': In 1972 Sandip Pakvasa and Kirthi Tennakone suggested that neutrinos may be massive and discussed consequences of massiveness, notably - astrophysical implications.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last=Pakvasa |display-authors=etal|first=S|year=1972|title=Neutrinos of Nonzero Rest Mass|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=28|issue=21|pages=1415–1418|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.28.1415|bibcode=1972PhRvL..28.1415P}}</ref> They pointed out the possibility assessing the neutrino mass by detecting the light and neutrino signals of supernova explosion.<ref name=":0" /> Tennakone has also examined macroscopic changes in linear and angular momentum associated with neutrino bursts from astrophysical systems.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Tennakone|first=K.|year=1975|title=Neutrino Processes and QSO's|journal=Nature|volume=254|issue=5499|pages=399–400|doi=10.1038/254399a0|bibcode=1975Natur.254..399T|s2cid=4166145}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Tennakone|first=K.|year=1972|title=Angular Momentum Changes in Astrophysical Processes due to Neutrino Emission|journal=Lettere al Nuovo Cimento|volume=583|issue=14|pages=583–584|doi=10.1007/BF02762057|bibcode=1972NCimL...3..583T|s2cid=189844669}}</ref>

''Condensed Matter Physics'': Kirthi Tennakone and co-workers pioneered<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Regan |display-authors=etal|first=B. O|year=1996|title=Efficient dye-sensitized charge separation in a wide band-gap|journal=Journal of Applied Physics|volume=80|issue=8|pages=4749–4754|doi=10.1063/1.363412}}</ref> the studies on semiconducting properties Copper(I) Thiocyanate, a rare example of a transparent p-type semiconductor, currently adopted in many devices and developed techniques of its deposition as thin films.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|last=Tennakone |display-authors=etal|first=K.|year=1984|title=Dye-sensitization of cuprous-thiocyanate photocathode in aqueous potassium thiocyanate|url=https://inis.iaea.org/search/searchsinglerecord.aspx?recordsFor=SingleRecord&RN=16040942|journal=Journal of the Electrochemical Society|volume=131|issue=7|pages=1574|via=INIS|doi=10.1149/1.2115912|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite journal|last=Tennekone |display-authors=etal|first=K.|year=1987|title=Semiconducting and Photoelectrochemical Properties of n- and p-Type -CuCNS|journal=Physica Status Solidi|volume=103|issue=2|pages=491–497|doi=10.1002/pssa.2211030220}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Tennekone |display-authors=etal|first=K.|year=1985|title=Superior Photocatalyst for Photooxidation of Water|journal=Chemical Physics Letters|volume=121|issue=6|pages=551–553|doi=10.1016/0009-2614(85)87139-6}}</ref> He has also worked on electrical conduction in unconventional materials, nanostructured films and electroceramics. Tennakone and co-workers introduced the idea of using crystal growth inhibitors to secure intimate contact and pore filling in nanostructured heterojunctions.

''Solar Energy Conversion and Photochemistry'': The concept of the dye-sensitized solid-state solar cell was first proposed by Tennakone et al. in a 1988 publication titled "Dye-sensitized solid-state solar cells".<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Tennekone |display-authors=etal|first=K.|year=1988|title=Dye-sensitised solid-state photovoltaic cells|journal=Semiconductor Science and Technology|volume=3|issue=4|pages=382–387|doi=10.1088/0268-1242/3/4/017|bibcode=1988SeScT...3..382T|s2cid=250919843 }}</ref> The invention of practical device based on the idea was also first reported by Tennakone et al. in 1995.<ref name="Tennekone 1995 1689–1693"/> Perovoskite solar cells are vigorously pursued nowadays are based on extremely thin layer of a low band gap semiconductor sandwiched between two nanostructured n and p type high band gap semiconductors, the concept  subsequently referred to as eta cell was reported by Tennakone et al. in 1998.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Tennakone |display-authors=etal|first=K.|year=1998|title=Nanoporous n-/selenium/p-CuCNS photovoltaic cell|journal=Journal of Physics D: Applied Physics|volume=31|issue=18|pages=2326–2330|doi=10.1088/0022-3727/31/18/019|bibcode=1998JPhD...31.2326T|s2cid=250769931 }}</ref> Dye-sensitized solar cells are generally based mesoporous  films of TiO<sub>2,</sub>.Tennakone’s group is also credited with development of a dye-sensitized cell of comparable efficiency adopting ZnO/SnO<sub>2</sub>composite films.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Tennekone |display-authors=etal|first=K.|year=1999|title=An efficient dye-sensitized photoelectrochemical solar cell made from oxides of tin and zinc|journal=Chemical Communications|issue=1|pages=1–16|doi=10.1039/A806801A}}</ref> Tennakone et al. has also studied the dye-sensitization  effect of plants derived   compounds.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Tennekone |display-authors=etal|first=K.|year=1996|title=Efficient photosensitization of nanocrystalline TiO2 films by tannins and related phenolic substances|journal=Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry|volume=94|issue=2–3|pages=217–220|doi=10.1016/1010-6030(95)04222-9}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Tennekone|first=K.|year=1997|title=Nanoporous TiO2 photoanode sensitized with the flower pigment cyanidin|journal=Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry|volume=108|issue=2–3|pages=193–195|doi=10.1016/S1010-6030(97)00090-7}}</ref>

''Biological Systems'': Tennakone has worked on the problem of biological L-D stereoselection<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Tennekone|first=K.|year=1990|title=Spontaneous breaking of the L, D symmetry in photolytic production and degradation of amino acids|journal=Origins of Life and Evolution of Biospheres|volume=20|issue=6|pages=515–519|doi=10.1007/BF01808198|bibcode=1990OLEB...20..515T|s2cid=22322710}}</ref> and right-left symmetries in plants., suggesting that former could be spontaneous symmetry breaking in prebiotic chemical reactions or rapid growth of  accidentally created, self-replicating handed  molecule in racemic prebiotic medium. According to his findings, right-left asymmetries in plants can be classified into three distinct categories. (a) All individuals of the species has same handedness. (b) Individuals have either right or left-handedness, occurring with equal probabilities. (c) Individuals have no definable handedness, but some organs possesses either right or left-handedness.

''Static Electricity'': Tennakone has published several papers in the area of static electricity including atmospheric effects.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Tennekone|first=K.|year=2011|title=Stable spherically symmetric static charge separated configurations in the atmosphere: Implications on ball lightning and earthquake lights|journal=Journal of Electrostatics|volume=69|issue=6|pages=638–640|doi=10.1016/j.elstat.2011.08.005}}</ref> Recently he has hypothesized that perchlorate in Mars could be produced by electrolysis of sodium chloride following static electrification regolith and moisture condensation.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Tennekone|first=K.|year=2016|title=Contact Electrification of Regolith Particles and Chloride Electrolysis: Synthesis of Perchlorates on Mars|journal=Astrobiology|volume=16|issue=10|pages=811–816|doi=10.1089/ast.2015.1424|pmid=27681637|bibcode=2016AsBio..16..811T}}</ref>

''Aluminum Leaching'': Tennakone observed that fluoride enhance leaching of aluminum from cooking utensils.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Tennekone |display-authors=etal|first=K.|year=1987|title=Aluminium leaching from cooking utensils|journal=Nature|volume=325|issue=6101|page=202|doi=10.1038/325202b0|pmid=3808018|bibcode=1987Natur.325..202T|s2cid=36433504|doi-access=free}}</ref> A subsequent work and repetition of the experiments by Tennakone et al.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Tennekone |display-authors=etal|first=K.|year=1987|title=Aluminium and cooking|url=https://www.nature.com/nature/journal/v329/n6138/abs/329398b0.html|journal=Nature|volume=329|issue=6138 |page=398 |doi=10.1038/329398b0 |bibcode=1987Natur.329..398T |via=Nature Publishing Group|url-access=subscription}}</ref> found that at 1ppm of F<sup>−</sup> leaching is not high as reported previously to pose a major toxicity issue. Later work of Tennakone<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Tennekone |display-authors=etal|first=K.|year=1988|title=Aluminium contamination from fluoride assisted dissolution of metallic aluminium|journal=Environmental Pollution|volume=49|issue=2|pages=133–143|doi=10.1016/0269-7491(88)90245-X|pmid=15092668}}</ref> and several other investigators have confirmed the enhancement Al leaching under culinary conditions, when F<sup>−</sup> concentration is 10 ppm or more.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Moody|display-authors=etal|first=G. H.|year=1990|title=Aluminium leaching and fluoride|url=http://citeweb.info/19900257827|journal=British Dental Journal|volume=169|issue=2|pages=47–50|via=BDJ|pmid=2390386|doi=10.1038/sj.bdj.4807270|s2cid=7796546|url-access=subscription|archive-date=2017-02-11|access-date=2017-02-09|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170211080851/http://citeweb.info/19900257827|url-status=dead}}</ref>
